recreation_prompt_markdown:
Recreate a compact mobile-friendly top-down arcade survival-crafting game called **Forge Run: Iron Trial**. The game should run in a single screen-oriented session where the player starts on a small procedurally generated island and tries to progress from primitive gathering to iron forging before an energy meter drains to zero. The core fantasy is being a lone adventurer-smith building up from scraps, placing a field furnace, entering a cave, and casting stronger tools under pressure.

Use a smooth-follow camera over a canvas-rendered world with chunky voxel-like or blocky visuals. The surface map should feel like an island with water around the edges, sand near the shoreline, grassy resource zones, and some mountain tiles that act as scenery or blockers. Somewhere away from spawn, place a cave entrance that transitions to a separate cave map containing walls, floor tiles, boulders, coal veins, iron veins, and a ladder back to the surface. Keep the presentation warm and forge-themed, with ember-orange highlights, dark night backgrounds, fantasy-smith UI framing, floating text popups, subtle hit particles, and dramatic start and game-over overlays.

Controls should be mobile-first. The player moves with an on-screen virtual joystick, and the game should also accept mouse/tap input for menus and the forging challenge. Regular harvesting should be proximity-based rather than requiring a separate attack button: when the player stands near a valid target and is not moving, the character automatically works on it over repeated ticks. This should make the loop feel accessible and arcade-like rather than simulation-heavy.

Build the progression around explicit tool and recipe gates. At the start, the player has no tools and can gather only simple materials: sticks from bushes, flint from pebbles, copper from small copper stones or surface copper veins, clay from shoreline clay spots, plus optional wool or meat from wandering sheep and cows. Trees should require an axe before they can be harvested for wood. Stone boulders, copper veins, and coal veins should require a better pick. Iron veins should be late-game and only realistically accessible once the player has progressed into the forge path. Resource drops should go into a visible HUD inventory that tracks raw and processed materials.

Add a crafting/forge button that opens a modal panel listing recipes. The player should be able to craft an axe from early materials, convert wood into planks, convert clay into molds, and build a field furnace on the surface. The furnace should not just be a recipe outcome; it should become a placed world object near the player and serve as a required proximity anchor for advanced smelting. The copper pick and iron pick should only be forgeable when the player is standing near the furnace and has the required ingredients.

Make the game loop follow this arc: gather basic surface supplies, craft an axe, harvest wood, turn wood into planks, gather enough clay to make molds and a furnace, collect enough copper for the first metal tool, place the furnace, forge a copper pick, search for and enter the cave, mine coal and iron underground, then return to complete the iron-forging stage. The run should end when energy reaches zero, and the final screen should summarize how much copper and iron the player banked.

Energy is the run timer and pressure system. It should drain steadily over time no matter what the player is doing, pushing them to keep moving and optimize routes. Collecting resource drops should restore a little energy, and meat should restore significantly more so animals function as opportunistic sustain. This should create a light survival feeling without turning the game into a punishing hardcore sim.

For advanced forging, add a short skill-based minigame instead of making metal tools craft instantly. When the player starts forging a copper pick or iron pick, hide the normal HUD and show an overlay with a mold silhouette and several highlighted circular targets. A timer bar counts down while the player taps the targets. Clearing all targets in time successfully completes the pour and awards the new tool; failing the timer causes the forge attempt to fail and should feel costly and tense. The copper version should use orange-hot visual cues, while the iron version should use cooler silver-white cues.

Include readable feedback everywhere: floating text for pickups and warnings like “NEED AXE” or “NEAR FURNACE REQUIRED,” tool icons that light up when acquired, disabled crafting buttons when requirements are not met, impact sounds during harvesting, success/failure sounds for crafting, looping background music, and a start screen that clearly teaches the run structure in a few steps. The overall tone should feel like a fast, polished, mobile survival-forging run with clear upgrade sequencing, simple exploration, and a satisfying climb from scavenging to ironworking.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## High-level code structure
This game is implemented as a single self-contained `index.html` file that includes:
- inline CSS for the full visual style, HUD, modal windows, joystick, and feedback overlays
- HTML for the canvas, mobile touch controls, start/game-over screens, HUD resource display, and crafting modal
- inline JavaScript module code that contains configuration, audio setup, procedural world generation, state management, update/render loops, crafting logic, and a forging minigame

The architecture is lightweight and monolithic, but still organized by commented sections:
- configuration/constants
- audio and feedback system
- global game state
- joystick/mobile input
- map generation
- update and interaction logic
- crafting and minigame logic
- rendering
- start/restart event wiring

## Game loop / state model
The game uses a `requestAnimationFrame` loop driven by a global `state.active` flag.

Primary state fields include:
- `mode`: `play`, `modal_open`, or `crafting_minigame`
- `currentMap`: `surface` or `cave`
- `inventory`: gathered and processed resources
- `tools`: `axe`, `pick`, `ironPick`
- `energy`: a time/turn pressure meter that drains steadily and is partially restored by collecting drops, especially meat
- `maps`: separate generated grids and entities for surface and cave
- `entities`: current map objects such as trees, ore, animals, furnace, entrance, ladder, and drops
- `particles`: floating text and impact particles
- `minigame`: temporary forging state for the pour/tap sequence

Loop behavior:
- in `play`, the game updates movement, auto-interactions, AI wandering, furnace proximity, particles, and energy drain
- in `modal_open`, the world effectively pauses except particles/UI remain visible
- in `crafting_minigame`, the main survival/gather loop is suspended and a tap-target forging sequence replaces it

## Player goals
The inferred progression goal is:
1. gather basic surface resources such as sticks, flint, clay, copper, wood, wool, and meat
2. craft an axe so trees become harvestable
3. process wood into planks and clay into molds
4. build a field furnace on the surface
5. use the furnace to forge a copper pick through a timed tapping minigame
6. locate and enter the cave
7. mine coal and iron
8. return to furnace access and forge the iron pick
9. survive as long as possible before energy reaches zero, while banking copper and iron as the score readout

The start screen strongly frames the run as a forge progression arc culminating in entering the cave and casting iron gear.

## Interaction pattern
The interaction model is primarily mobile-first:
- virtual joystick for movement
- proximity-based auto-harvesting when standing still near an entity
- one-button access to the crafting/forge modal
- tap/click interaction during the forging minigame

Interaction heuristics:
- moving navigates the world; stopping near a valid target triggers repeated harvesting attempts
- some nodes are always harvestable, while others require specific tool upgrades
- cave entrance and ladder are context portals between maps
- crafting buttons are enabled/disabled dynamically based on resources, tool ownership, and furnace proximity
- the forging step for advanced tools adds a skill check instead of immediate crafting

## Core systems
### 1. Procedural overworld and cave generation
- surface island-like map with water, sand, grass, and mountain zones
- randomized placement of resource nodes and animals
- cave map with walls, floor, coal, iron, boulders, and ladder

### 2. Resource harvesting
Entities have HP and are destroyed through repeated hits.
Drops include:
- sticks from bushes
- flint from pebbles
- copper from copper stones/veins
- clay from shoreline clay spots
- wood from trees
- coal and iron from cave veins
- wool and meat from animals

### 3. Tool gating
Progression is unlocked through explicit tool requirements:
- trees require axe or iron pick
- boulders/copper/coal require copper or iron pick
- iron requires at least the copper pick

### 4. Crafting and processing
Recipes transform gathered resources into:
- axe
- planks
- mold
- furnace
- copper pick
- iron pick

### 5. Furnace proximity rule
Advanced smelting only becomes available when the player is physically near the placed furnace, creating spatial staging around the base.

### 6. Forging minigame
Copper and iron pick creation trigger a timed tapping challenge over a mold silhouette. Success awards the tool; timeout wastes the attempt.

### 7. Energy/time pressure
Energy drains automatically over time and creates run tension. Collecting drops restores some energy, with meat giving a larger refill.

### 8. Feedback/presentation systems
- floating combat/resource text
- hit particles
- success/fail GIF reactions
- background music and SFX
- HUD inventory and tool indicators
- start and game-over overlays

## Inferred genre / gameplay shape
Strongest inferred shape:
- survival-crafting runner with light exploration
- top-down gathering/progression game
- arcade survival loop rather than deep simulation

It feels like a compact, mobile-friendly crafting survival run:
- gather quickly
- upgrade tools in sequence
- place a furnace base
- delve into a cave for higher-tier resources
- race against an energy clock

## Gameplay heuristic
The intended player heuristic appears to be:
- secure basic materials immediately near spawn
- craft the axe early to unlock wood economy
- convert wood to planks and gather enough clay for mold + furnace
- place the furnace as a progression anchor before serious cave mining
- collect easy copper on the surface for the first advanced tool
- enter the cave only once the copper pick route is realistic
- hunt animals opportunistically for energy sustain
- treat the iron stage as the late-run objective and score expression

## Confidence notes
Confidence is fairly high because the code exposes explicit systems, recipes, map transitions, UI labels, and objective framing in the start screen.
Lower-confidence areas:
- whether the game has a true “win” state; the code suggests no formal victory screen, only survival until energy depletion
- whether “banked” copper/iron on the game-over screen is intended as final score or simply an inventory summary
- whether animal harvesting is meant to imply hunting or abstract gathering, since interactions are highly stylized and non-realistic

selected_categories.reasoning: The game centers on staying alive under a constantly draining energy meter while gathering resources, crafting upgrades, and extending the run through efficient play.
A large part of play is collecting, storing, and converting many resource types into processed goods and new tools through a visible inventory-driven progression chain.
The player must budget sticks, flint, clay, wood, planks, molds, copper, coal, and iron across tightly gated recipes and energy pressure.
Both the surface island and cave are procedurally generated, and the player explores them to locate resource nodes, the cave entrance, and efficient harvesting routes.
The harvesting loop is partly passive and repeated over time while near targets, and the forging sequence uses rapid tapping, but the game is not primarily an idle or click-economy title.

uncertainty_notes: The game overlaps with crafting, survival, and light exploration, but the provided category universe does not include a direct crafting-survival action-adventure label.

Clicker game is only a weak fit included as the fifth-best available match because some interactions are repetitive/tap-based, yet movement and spatial traversal matter much more than in a pure clicker.
Endless runner, lane runner, and neon/void runner categories are not strong matches despite the title including the word 'Run'; the actual gameplay is top-down gathering and forging.
